name: Arctic Ocean
genZNote: The Arctic is the smallest, coldest ocean — and the one changing fastest, because its sea ice is melting quickly enough to open up shipping routes that didn't reliably exist a generation ago.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Extent
bullets: The smallest and shallowest of the major oceans, centred roughly on the North Pole.
Largely covered by sea ice for much of the year, though the ice-covered extent has been shrinking over recent decades.
Connects to the Pacific Ocean through the narrow Bering Strait and to the Atlantic Ocean through the wider waters around Greenland and Norway.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries With Coastlines On It
bullets: The five "Arctic coastal states": Russia, Canada, the United States (via Alaska), Norway, and Denmark (via Greenland).
Iceland, Sweden and Finland are also Arctic Council members though not all have a direct Arctic Ocean coastline.
No country owns the Arctic Ocean itself — coastal states hold exclusive economic zones extending from their coastlines, with some areas still under international negotiation.

sections.heading: 🚢 Trade, Resources & Strategic Importance
bullets: The Northern Sea Route (along Russia's Arctic coast) and the Northwest Passage (through Canada's Arctic archipelago) are increasingly discussed as shorter alternatives to traditional Europe-Asia shipping lanes, though both remain seasonal and ice-dependent.
Believed to hold significant untapped oil, gas and mineral resources beneath the seabed, which is part of why Arctic territorial claims are strategically sensitive.
The Arctic Council is the main intergovernmental forum for cooperation among Arctic states.
Shrinking sea ice is gradually making Arctic shipping routes more viable for longer parts of the year, with real economic and environmental trade-offs.

sections.heading: 🐻‍❄️ Marine Ecology & Environmental Concerns
bullets: Supports a distinct cold-water ecosystem: polar bears, seals, walruses, narwhals and Arctic seabirds, many dependent on sea ice for hunting or breeding.
Warming in the Arctic is occurring faster than the global average, a phenomenon known as Arctic amplification.
Shrinking summer sea-ice extent is one of the most visible, widely tracked indicators of global climate change.
Increased shipping and resource extraction interest raises concerns about oil-spill risk and habitat disruption in a slow-to-recover cold-water environment.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Arctic Ocean is Earth's smallest and shallowest ocean, centred on the North Pole and bordered by five Arctic coastal states.
keyFacts: Smallest, shallowest major ocean; centred on the North Pole.
Five Arctic coastal states: Russia, Canada, USA, Norway, Denmark (Greenland).
Northern Sea Route and Northwest Passage are emerging seasonal shipping lanes.
Warming faster than the global average (Arctic amplification).
commonConfusion: The Northern Sea Route (via Russia) and the Northwest Passage (via Canada) are two different routes — don't merge them into one.

highYieldFacts: Smallest, shallowest ocean; centred on North Pole.
Five Arctic coastal states; Arctic Council is the main cooperation forum.
Sea-ice shrinkage is opening seasonal shipping routes.
commonTraps: Don't assume Arctic shipping routes are open year-round — both major routes remain seasonal and ice-dependent.
mustRemember: Arctic Ocean = smallest/shallowest; 5 coastal states; Northern Sea Route + Northwest Passage; fastest-warming ocean region.
